rules.name: Listening socket owned by a process in a user-writable path
rules.description: A process whose executable lives in a user-writable directory is listening on a non-loopback address.
rules.rationale: A listener outside loopback can accept connections from the network. Per-user server software (development servers, sync tools) also listens, so an unexpected owner is the signal, not the port.
evidenceRequirements: Process executable path for the owning PID
rules.titleTemplate: {ProcessName} listens on port {LocalPort} from a user-writable path
falsePositives: Developer tools and local web servers
Peer-to-peer or sync clients installed per user
rules.recommendedNextStep: Identify the process, its parent and start time, and whether the port is reachable from other hosts (host firewall rules). Check for matching persistence findings.
rules.remediation: If the listener is not approved, an authorized responder could block the port at the network layer and investigate the process. This toolkit never changes the system; any action is a manual decision for an authorized responder after validation.
limitations: A listening port by itself is not a technique, so this rule has no ATT&CK mapping.

rules.name: Established outbound connection from a script host or proxy-execution binary
rules.description: wscript, cscript, mshta, regsvr32, rundll32, certutil or bitsadmin has an established connection to a public IP address.
rules.rationale: These binaries rarely need direct internet access in normal use, and attackers use them to fetch or run remote content. Some enterprise software legitimately drives them over the network.
evidenceRequirements: Established TCP connections with owning process
Process name for the owning PID
falsePositives: Software deployment or licensing tools that call these binaries
Windows components that briefly use rundll32 for network features
rules.recommendedNextStep: Look up the remote address in your threat intelligence and DNS/proxy logs, find the parent process and command line, and review what the process loaded.
rules.remediation: If the connection is not approved, an authorized responder could block the destination and contain the host after preserving evidence. This toolkit never changes the system; any action is a manual decision for an authorized responder after validation.
limitations: A connection is a point-in-time observation; an unfamiliar address is not proof of malicious activity.

rules.name: Outbound connection from a process in a user-writable path
rules.description: A process running from a user-writable directory has an established connection to a public IP address.
rules.rationale: This is a broad contextual signal: most per-user software (browsers, chat, sync) behaves this way. It is disabled by default and is meant to be enabled when investigating a specific host.
evidenceRequirements: Established TCP connections with owning process
Process executable path for the owning PID
falsePositives: Browsers, collaboration tools, update checkers and any per-user application
rules.recommendedNextStep: Use as context: combine with execution and persistence findings for the same process before drawing conclusions.
rules.remediation: No action is recommended from this finding alone. This toolkit never changes the system; any action is a manual decision for an authorized responder after validation.
limitations: Disabled by default (ruleOverrides can enable it). Unusual endpoints or ports are not proof of malicious behavior.
